findings.reason: The protected SQL solution sums total rest, paid, canceled, and refunded monetary amounts per product. It performs a LEFT JOIN from Product to Invoice on product_id, groups by product_id and name, uses COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) to replace null sums for products without invoices, and orders by p.name ASC. The query runs in O(I + P log P) time and O(P) space; no candidate is required.
LEFT JOIN ensures all catalog products are retained regardless of invoice history, and COALESCE guarantees 0 defaults for missing amounts.

Scanning P products and I invoices takes O(P + I) time for hash join and grouping, plus O(P log P) time for sorting results by product name. Space is O(P) for aggregation buffers. Complexity evidence is bounded-domain certified and hash-bound.
Accepts Product and Invoice tables, returning columns name, rest, paid, canceled, and refunded sorted by name ASC.

The approach accurately details catalog preservation via LEFT JOIN, COALESCE-guarded SUM aggregation, name-based output sorting, and O(I + P log P) time / O(P) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover pre-aggregating invoices subquery options, INNER JOIN product omission defects, correlated aggregate subquery inefficiencies, zero-invoice product defaults, zero-value invoice handling, and primary key gap independence.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical LEFT JOIN COALESCE SUM query with SHA-256 digest 9ef32598bd75f85953bf99cdb5ab074998aca536641cf3d8bab7263209990f3c. Verified submission remains untouched.

Statement structure and factual evidence confirmed Product and Invoice interface, three examples, three constraints, and 5 local tables. Bound to content SHA-256 808f370200199da7290ce93a5c707cd2b4a61cac66ac35eab98364bbd4197515.
